- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line or code reference: line 18690-18691 (uncapped diff fetch: PR_DIFF="$(gh_retry gh api "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/pulls/${RB_PR}" -H 'Accept: application/vnd.github.diff' ...)") feeding line 18953 (head -1000 <<< "${PR_DIFF}" inside the review-blocked judge prompt assembly that is exec'd through codex)
  Problem: This PR fixes the wave-judge prompt overflow (byte caps after the 500-line cap, because a single minified-bundle line of 44-66 KB defeats any line cap), but the poller-side review-blocked judge path in the same file embeds a PR diff with only a head -1000 line cap and no byte cap. The incident this PR cites (run 35425771769, project #3928) was caused by exactly this input class — committed Cloudflare Worker dist refresh PRs whose diffs are a handful of 40-70 KB single lines. One thousand such lines is tens of MB, far over codex's 1,048,576-character turn/start stdin cap.
  Why it fails at runtime: if any PR carrying large minified-bundle diffs (the same PR shape documented in this PR's own changelog, #4416/#4425) transitions to ai:review-blocked on an orchestrator project, the review-blocked judge prompt assembled at lines 18934-18953 exceeds the codex stdin cap and every judge attempt dies with "Input exceeds the maximum length of 1048576 characters" before the model runs — the identical failure mode this PR eliminates for the wave judge, one code path over. The new _judge_truncate_pr_diff_file helper could be applied to this fetch with a few lines. This is a pre-existing adjacent site, not introduced by this diff, but it is the same defect class in the same file with the fix pattern now available in-tree.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3

- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Location: _judge_truncate_pr_diff_file, final else branch (~lines 230-235)
  Issue: if both the python3 truncation and the head -c fallback fail, the helper removes the temp file and returns 0, leaving the diff file untruncated; the caller then logs "diff truncated from X to Y bytes" and embeds the full over-cap diff, silently reintroducing the exact prompt-overflow failure this PR fixes, with a misleading log line.
  Suggested minimal fix: in the final else branch, write the sentinel into the diff file before returning, e.g. printf '%s' "(diff unavailable)" > "${diff_path}" — mirroring the double-failure handling in scripts/review_rb_judge.sh line 1092 — so the caller embeds a bounded sentinel instead of an untruncated diff.
  HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1
